title: Publish and verify the existing prototype baseline
body:
Get the current local prototype into the repository so subsequent issues have a shared baseline.

**Done when**
- The source, tests, README and workflow are present on the default branch.
- A fresh checkout can generate the Physlib snapshot, run tests and serve the app.
- Existing source-scan limitations are documented.

title: Compare direct import extraction with importGraph
body:
Evaluate our source scanner against Lean-aware import extraction at a pinned Physlib commit and toolchain.

**Done when**
- A reproducible comparison covers representative files in Physlib, PhyslibAlpha and QuantumInfo, including umbrella modules.
- Differences and their causes are recorded, with a recommendation on which extractor to use.

Reference: https://github.com/leanprover-community/import-graph

title: Record snapshot toolchain and extraction diagnostics
body:
Make the published dataset's provenance and completeness inspectable.

**Done when**
- The snapshot records Physlib SHA, Lean toolchain, generation time, extractor identity/version and counts.
- Unresolved local imports and API-map references are reported separately from external imports.
- The interface exposes freshness and a link to the exact source commit.

title: Define a versioned graph data contract
body:
Document a machine-readable contract for modules, declarations, API maps and typed relationships.

**Done when**
- IDs, edge direction, node/edge types and provenance fields are specified with a small example.
- The contract distinguishes observed facts, curated references and inferred candidates.
- Version and compatibility rules are documented without requiring a particular graph database.

title: Validate generated snapshots before publication
body:
Add checks that prevent a malformed or incomplete snapshot from replacing the previous published version.

**Done when**
- Schema version, unique IDs, references and source metadata are checked.
- Failures produce actionable diagnostics and fail the publication job.
- Tests cover a valid snapshot and representative invalid input.

title: Pilot lean-vouch declaration extraction on a Physlib area
body:
Evaluate Jonathan Jeffrey's lean-vouch against a small, representative Physlib area at a pinned commit.

**Done when**
- Record setup, toolchain, build time, output format and a reproducible command or procedure.
- Inspect a few declaration statements and dependencies against Lean/source.
- Document coverage, edge direction and integration questions for discussion with Jonathan.

Reference: https://github.com/jjeffrey/lean-vouch

title: Compare result-graph and lean-vouch outputs on the pilot
body:
Compare the tools on the same pinned area and declarations before selecting an extraction interface.

**Done when**
- Compare coverage, dependency direction, statement/proof categories, provenance and practical build costs.
- Document meaningful differences and a recommendation; do not assume differently defined edges are equivalent.

Reference: https://github.com/PierreSenellart/result-graph

title: Add an adapter for declaration graph snapshots
body:
Using the pilot's chosen interface, convert declaration data into the versioned graph contract.

**Done when**
- Declaration IDs, kinds, source modules, available statements/docstrings and dependency edges are exported with provenance.
- Unsupported or unavailable fields are explicit.
- Fixture-based tests cover direction and representative declarations.

The implementation choice follows the pilot; do not assume a specific upstream tool is compatible until tested.

title: Resolve API-map references to declaration nodes
body:
Connect existing API-map Lean references to the declaration graph.

**Done when**
- Store explicit map-to-file and resolvable map-to-declaration links with reference location.
- Preserve ambiguous or unresolved references as diagnostics rather than guessing.
- Cover repeated references, notation and instance-type entries with tests.

title: Show typed relationships and their provenance
body:
Make relationship semantics visible in the explorer.

**Done when**
- Users can distinguish imports, API-map references and available statement/proof dependency types.
- An edge's source, extraction method and revision are accessible.
- Relationship filters do not silently combine distinct edge types.

title: Add a focused declaration dependency view
body:
Provide a readable neighborhood around one declaration.

**Done when**
- Users can switch between prerequisites and reverse dependents and change the depth.
- Size limits and omitted nodes are visible.
- A declaration links to its statement and exact-revision source when available.

title: Add a browsable hierarchy and shareable graph links
body:
Help users navigate large graphs and return to the same view.

**Done when**
- A keyboard-accessible expandable hierarchy exposes libraries, directories and modules.
- A URL restores the selected node and relevant view settings.
- Missing or renamed targets produce a useful message.

title: Show paths and potential impact between graph nodes
body:
Help users understand how nodes relate and which results may be affected by changes.

**Done when**
- Show an explainable dependency path with edge types and direction.
- Show bounded reverse reachability and indicate truncation.
- Explain that reachability is potential impact, not proof of breakage.

title: Compare two graph snapshots
body:
Provide a descriptive diff between two indexed Physlib revisions.

**Done when**
- Identify added and removed nodes and edges, with both revision IDs.
- Report changes in available declaration statements when the extractor supports it.
- Treat possible renames as candidates, not definitive identity matches.

title: Evaluate lean-vouch review and freshness overlays
body:
Investigate displaying attributed review information without reimplementing lean-vouch's workflow.

**Done when**
- Document available review data, attribution, licensing, freshness semantics and integration constraints.
- Show a small example or mockup distinguishing review marks from proof validity.
- Record a recommendation and unresolved questions; do not import private review data by default.

title: Investigate linking PhyslibSearch results to graph nodes
body:
Evaluate interoperability with Physlib's existing declaration search before creating a second search service.

**Done when**
- Document available links/API, identifiers, coverage and snapshot/version behavior.
- Demonstrate or specify mapping a search result to a graph declaration; handle missing and mismatched revisions.
- Record any dependencies on the PhyslibSearch maintainers.

Reference: https://github.com/Kernel-Science/physlibsearch

title: Evaluate Loogle and duplicate-declaration checks on the pilot
body:
Assess existing tools for helping contributors discover related declarations.

**Done when**
- Run representative Loogle searches and Mathlib DuplicateDecls checks on a pinned pilot or document a blocker.
- Record useful matches, false positives and cases not detected.
- Propose a review workflow that treats results as candidates rather than certifying novelty.

title: Prototype explainable module clustering
body:
Compare directory organization with a graph-derived grouping for exploration.

**Done when**
- Record the algorithm, input edge types and treatment of umbrella/foundational modules.
- Show how groups differ from directories for a representative sample.
- Make clear that clusters and centrality are exploratory, not scientific importance or automatic priority.

title: Publish a versioned machine-readable graph export
body:
Make graph snapshots usable by other tools and coding assistants.

**Done when**
- Publish documented, versioned data with source and extraction provenance.
- Supply an example query or small client that finds a node and its direct typed edges.
- Keep generated data separate from curated API-map or review content.

title: Evaluate navigation and retrieval with Physlib contributors
body:
Create a small repeatable evaluation based on real contributor questions.

**Done when**
- Collect a documented set of tasks with known relevant files or declarations.
- Compare graph-assisted discovery with simple text/name search for the same tasks.
- Record findings, limitations and follow-up improvements without claiming novelty guarantees.

title: Harden upstream refresh and publication
body:
Keep the graph synchronized with Physlib master while preserving a known-good snapshot.

**Done when**
- Scheduled and manual refreshes build against a pinned upstream SHA; unchanged commits can be skipped.
- Failed validation leaves the last successful version available and exposes failure/freshness information.
- Concurrent jobs cannot publish an older snapshot over a newer one.
- Document a maintainer-coordinated event trigger for near-immediate refresh, with polling as fallback.

title: Evaluate integration with the Physlib website
body:
Determine how to make the explorer accessible from physlib.io after validating the prototype.

**Done when**
- Confirm the current website source, hosting and deployment process with maintainers.
- Compare a link, subdomain and integrated page against maintenance and accessibility needs.
- Document the recommended integration and its ownership; do not change the live site as part of this investigation.
